title: The normalized finite dualizing maps satisfy the recorded stage tower equation
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l different from D.p, an algebraic closure Ω of Q_l in an independent universe, and a separated finite-type D.k-scheme X. Let F be a Finite datum with the actual raw rational finite stages and normalized scalar comparisons of [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data]. For every E ≤ L ≤ M in the index of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], put W_E = localization_E((F.omega E).omega) and o_h = operationStageTransitionIso(h).app(W_E) followed by (F.scalar E L h).omega. Then T_k(o_h.hom) ≫ o_k.hom = assoc(h,k).hom.app(W_E) ≫ o_(h.trans k).hom in the rational M-stage category. No FiniteCoherent hypothesis and no descended dual, descended omega, or descended evaluation is used.

proof.text: For the three finite coefficient fields choose the actual integral dualizing data F.omega. The composition clause of IntegralFiniteExtension.comparison_composition gives scalar(u(E,L)) followed by u(L,M) equal to the balanced tensor associator followed by u(E,M). Its presentation naturality hypotheses are supplied by IntegralHom.evaluation_naturality. This step uses only the u component of CompositionConclusion.

Replace the hom of each F.scalar.omega by its localized integral u using F.normalized. Rational scalar extension maps a localized integral morphism to the localization of its integral scalar extension, and localization preserves composition. The defining normalization of sfRationalScalarComp is the localization of the same completed balanced tensor associator. The preceding integral equality therefore gives the rational omega tower equation, with the prescribed rational scalar associator, not an arbitrary associator.

Use coefficientInclusion_laws to identify the composite field inclusion with the direct inclusion. The chosen associator equals scalarAssociator by associator_existsUnique. Transport the rational equation along the transition equalities defining operationStageTransitionIso. Naturality moves the intermediate equality isomorphism through the omega map, cancelling it; the remaining equation is exactly the displayed stage equation. This works for identity inclusions, the zero object, and empty X.

theorem finiteOmegaStageComparison_tower (F : Finite D l hl Ω X)
    {E L M : Index l Ω} (h : E ≤ L) (k : L ≤ M) :
    ((stageSystem l Ω X).T k).map (finiteOmegaStageComparison D l hl Ω X F h).hom ≫
        (finiteOmegaStageComparison D l hl Ω X F k).hom =
      ((stageSystem l Ω X).assoc h k).hom.app
          ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) X).obj
            (F.omega E).omega) ≫
        (finiteOmegaStageComparison D l hl Ω X F (h.trans k)).hom
